findings.evidence: Every measuring command was refused by the producer's shell policy. The entry is honest about this and labels the estimates. But D145's disk budget and alternative e still rest on estimates, and design line 104 ('Build job 1 measures them') is still pending. Getting real numbers needs a role or job type whose shell can run sccache, du, df and git worktree. A third producer retry won't produce them.

findings.summary: The suggested S command can under-count on a large file list.
findings.evidence: `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 du -ck | tail -n 1`: if xargs splits the list into several du calls, each prints its own total, and `tail -n 1` keeps only the last one. Simpler and correct: `git ls-files -z | du -ck --files0-from=- | tail -n 1`, or `du -sk --exclude=.git .` in a fresh worktree.

summary: The retry meets the accepted reading, so the verdict is pass. The new '### A1 measurements' section in docs/decisions.md has no blank or "not measured"-only fields, which was the problem with the first attempt. Each field gives the exact command tried (`sccache --show-stats`, `df -h .`, `git worktree add ../wt-a1 HEAD`, `du -sk .`) and the error text that refused it. It also says plainly that the cause of D84's 0 hits was not found and lists what was tried. T (about 6 GB) and S (about 0.2 GB) are quoted from docs/design/async-drain.md lines 103-104 and labeled as estimates. I read those lines, and the figures match. D145 is now marked accepted by the brain under Sri's delegation (2026-10-29) in decisions.md, and the status line in the design doc agrees. The CHANGELOG entry says outright that the A1 entry is not a measurement. Only the three listed files changed. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and both pass. I ran them because Athena's records show both as skipped. Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` passed (1665 tests). Two caveats: no real number was measured, because the producer's shell blocks sccache, du, df and git worktree, so job 1 of the design still needs a role that can run those tools. Also, the S command suggested for a later job can under-count.
